meta.title: Baidu DuMate for DSH
meta.description:
[No longer maintained — forks welcome]

Turn the Baidu DuMate account you are already signed into into a model provider inside DSH: its models show up directly in the picker, and credit balance, spend detail and the daily check-in sit on the composer — no more switching between two windows. Chat goes through DuMate's own cloud model gateway by default, so the desktop app does not need to be running.

Install: download the tag archive from GitHub, extract it, pick that folder in Plugins → Add plugin, then restart DSH. Requires DSH ≥ 0.2.2 (below that the host silently skips the whole bundle without an error). Exact steps are the first section of the README.

Two ways to sign in: if the desktop app is installed you fill in nothing; otherwise paste two cookies (bce-sessionid and bce-user-info — the measured minimum) under Settings → DuMate → Account. The plugin does not register accounts, does not sign in for you and does not share credentials; every call spends credits from your own account. Cookies are stored encrypted on this machine only — plaintext is never written to disk, logged or sent to the page, and read paths never write the key file. The single write operation is claiming the daily check-in, off by default and only sent when you press the button or explicitly enable it.

Two things we do not inflate: the personal-edition catalog publishes no per-model credit multiplier, so none is shown; model ids are DuMate SKU labels, not vendor model names (measured: glm-5 is served by DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash) — the plugin records the real backend only after the upstream reports it, and never names a model on the upstream's behalf. This is an unofficial third-party integration and can break if the upstream tightens; assess the account risk yourself. Full data boundaries are in docs/PRIVACY.md inside the package.

The author hit the ceiling here: the upstream per-account rate limit cannot be worked around (the exact threshold is not published and I could not reproduce a stable number), an account pool and automatic failover were never implemented, and macOS/Linux have unit tests but no real hardware. The code, docs and every measured fact stay in the repository under MIT — fork it. Start with docs/FOR-FORKERS.md.
